context: The maximum capacity problem gives the heights of 8 vertical boards in the array ht = [3, 8, 5, 2, 7, 7, 3, 4], indexed from 0 to 7. For any pair of boards [i, j], the container's width is the index difference j - i. Its water level is limited by the shorter board, min(ht[i], ht[j]). In this definition, boards between the two ends do not block the water or reduce the area.
description: The vertical axis shows board heights from 0 to 8, and the horizontal axis shows array indices from 0 to 7. A vertical bar at each index represents the corresponding board. The boards at indices 1 (height 8) and 5 (height 7) and the horizontal axis between them are highlighted in a dark color. A translucent light blue rectangle between the boards shows the water, 7 units high and 4 units wide. A blue-violet “Shorter board” label and a horizontal dashed line mark the water limit at height 7 on the vertical axis. The bottom label reads “Maximum capacity = (5 - 1) × 7 = 28.”

frames.explanation: The shorter board on the right limits the water level to 7. The distance between the boards is 5 - 1 = 4, so the area is 4 × 7 = 28. The “Shorter board” label sits beside height 7 on the vertical axis to indicate the water level. It does not sit above index 5. This figure shows the maximum and the pair that achieves it. Later figures show how other pairs are ruled out.
frames.title: Maximum capacity between two boards

summary: Choose two boards to form a container. Its capacity is the height of the shorter board times the distance between them. The goal is to find the pair with the greatest capacity.
title: Maximum capacity between two boards
